sections.overall: To say All In: London '26 was an eventful, successful show is an understatement! So many highlights to choose from but the very best match of the week (and year, so far!) was Will Ospreay vs Kenny Omega (9.64). Seeing Will be crowned World Heavyweight Champion for the first time, in front of his home crowd... the kick out of the One-winged Angel.... plus so much more. The Women's World Title match was also amazing (see that Division's breakdown for more!). Meanwhile, we had very average Dynamite and Collision shows this week, a relatively minor point on what was a huge week for AEW.
sections.mens: Other Men's matches that stood out were Kazuchika Okada reclaiming his International Title in the 3 Way with Kyle Fletcher and Konosuke Takeshita (8.56). Although not in the same league as the other best matches, it helped push Kyle back into 'Platinum' status. Jon Moxley vs Nigel McGuinness was also better than expected (8.1). Going back to the All In main event, it is worth noting that both Omega and Ospreay have been reinstated to 'Platinum', the former at #1, a new all-time peak for him in possibly his last AEW match.
sections.womens: Mercedes Mone vs Willow Nightingale absolutely ruled (9.33)! The only Women's match rated higher than this in AEW history was the 'Hollywood Ending' from last year, which shows you how exceptionally well the title rivals performed. Mercedes is back to 'Gold' with an all-time peak reached. Willow also reaches an all-time peak and #2 in the rankings. Gone from the rankings is Thekla - although returning at All In in person - 6 weeks of inactivity means she drops out. Hopefully she will be back soon!
sections.menstag: Cage and Copeland's defense against The Young Bucks was a decent but not as strong as we hoped (7.63). The latter have gone quite a few weeks without a 'top' i.e. 8+ rated-match. There were various of Men's Tag Teams featured across the week in other matches, but none that especially stood out.
sections.womenstag: Although Divine Dominion's long reign being vanquished by The Brawling Birds led to decent gains, it wasn't the epic showdown it could've been (6.46). Still, it was great to see all four women feautured prominently on the biggest show of the year.
sections.trios: Welcome to The New Level! Their Trio team with Swerve Strickland was one of those anticipated 'surprises' that went down beautifully in the Pre-show main event/spill over match to the actual show. Although we had ANOTHER title change, the sheer number of regular teams means the division is genuinely heating up!
